correctness.rationale: For all r>=2, universal-homogeneous Henson one-point extension diagrams identify types with K_r-free induced subsets. On K_(a_i), the forbidden sets are exactly those hitting all shores. The exact product Q has q_r=product a_i and, after z=e^t-1, its formal logarithm recovers first r-1 even power sums of shores via nonzero Bernoulli coefficients using only q_r..q_(3r-2). Newton plus q_r squared reconstructs a_i squared. For r=3 exact q3,q4,q5 expressions provide sum, product and pairwise sum. The bounded exhaustive n<=13 integer-triple enumeration proves unique first collision, and singleton padding shifts the discrepancy. The actual bundled checker independently counted 184 direct finite types and reconstructed 1,465 profiles with exact rational arithmetic, returning VERIFY_OK. Finite computations are not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The graded one-point spectrum is a natural definable invariant, and identifying how much of it recovers structure is a genuine information-theoretic inverse question. The rank-dependent uniform cutoff independent of the number n of named parameters is a structural reconstruction theorem, not a rote evaluation of the known product. The sharp r=3 result locates the precise first grade and first parameter order where reconstruction fails, provides two nonisomorphic collision graphs, and extends the impossibility of too-short prefixes to every larger clique rank. This has a plausible role in finite-base model-theoretic equivalence and efficient invariant recovery. It does not rely on merely reproducing a known count.
